extracted.intended_audience: IP lawyers, patent agents, patent professionals, and AIPLA members (those interested in economic/market data for IP practice)
extracted.subtask_description: Extraction of the survey metrics and dimensions used in the AIPLA 2023 Economic Survey reporting statistics for patent/IP practitioners (questions on remote work, income, billing, practice composition, demographics, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: If you worked remotely in 2022, what percent of your time? (Q3b)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent-reported percent of time worked remotely in 2022. Shown as mean (average), median (midpoint), and number of individuals; reported overall and broken down by practice categories/roles (All Individuals, Primary Practice, Solo Practitioner, Private Firm roles, Corporate roles, PTO, Government IP, Other).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statistics provided: mean, median, and N for each role/category. Used to assess extent of remote work across types of IP practitioners.

rubrics_metrics.name: If you worked remotely in 2022, how many miles away is your remote work location from your office location? (Q3c)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent-reported distance in miles between remote work location and office location for those who worked remotely in 2022. Shown as mean (average), median (midpoint), and number of individuals; broken down by practice category/role.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides distributional statistics (mean, median, N) by role to evaluate how geographically separated remote work was from offices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do you plan to work or continue working remotely in 2023? (Q4a)
rubrics_metrics.description: Planned continuation of remote work in 2023; binary Yes/No percentages reported for overall respondents and by practice categories/roles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reported as percent Yes and No and total count for each group; useful for forecasting remote-work persistence by role.

rubrics_metrics.name: If you plan to continue working remotely in 2023, what percent of your time? (Q4b)
rubrics_metrics.description: For respondents planning to continue remote work in 2023, the percent of time expected to be remote. Presented as mean, median, and N by practice category/role.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distributional measures show expected remote-work intensity going forward.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do you work full-time as defined by your firm/company? (Q5)
rubrics_metrics.description: Self-reported full-time status (Yes/No) according to employer definition; percentages and counts provided overall and by practice category/role.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicates part-time vs full-time workforce composition across IP practice types.

rubrics_metrics.name: Major field of academic study (Q11)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondents' primary non-law academic field (e.g., Biology/Biotechnology, Electrical Engineering, Mechanical/Aerospace, Chemistry, Computer Science/Software Engineering, etc.). Reported as percentages across categories and counts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Breaks out technical backgrounds of IP professionals; useful to profile technical specialization and hiring pools.

rubrics_metrics.name: Total gross income in calendar year 2022 from primary practice - Full-time only (Q13a)
rubrics_metrics.description: Total gross income from primary practice for full-time respondents. Reported with first quartile (25%), median, mean, third quartile (75%), and number of individuals; presented overall and by practice category/role and many demographic/practice subgroups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Income distribution statistics used to characterize earnings across roles, specialties, locations, and experience levels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amount of year-end cash bonus (Q13b)
rubrics_metrics.description: Year-end cash bonus amounts for applicable respondents, with first quartile, median, mean, third quartile and N, broken down by practice category/role.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides compensation component beyond base income; reported for groups where bonus is applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Employer's 2022 contribution to 401(k)/403(b) retirement plans (Q14)
rubrics_metrics.description: Employer contribution amounts to retirement/savings plans in 2022. Reported with first quartile, median, mean, third quartile and N across respondent groups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Captures employer retirement benefit contributions by role and subgroup.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expected total cash income for 2023 - Full-time only (Q15)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondents' expected total cash income for 2023. Reported as first quartile (25%), mean, median, third quartile (75%), and N by role/subgroup.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to gauge income expectations and trends year-over-year across IP practice categories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Total gross income for 2022 from primary practice - Part-time only (Q13a)
rubrics_metrics.description: Total gross income for part-time respondents, with quartiles, median, mean and N across applicable groups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analogous income distribution for part-time practitioners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expected total cash income for 2023 - Part-time only (Q15)
rubrics_metrics.description: Expected 2023 cash income for part-time respondents, reported with quartiles, mean, median and N.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Forecasts for part-time practitioners' earnings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Full-time IP lawyers and patent agents at all locations (Q19)
rubrics_metrics.description: Counts/statistics describing the number of full-time IP lawyers and patent agents at respondents' firms/corporations (mean, median, quartiles, N), with breakdowns by location, technical specialization, and firm size categories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Characterizes firm size and in-house IP team scale across geographies and practice specialties.

rubrics_metrics.name: How many billable hours did you record in 2022? (Q32)
rubrics_metrics.description: Self-reported billable hours recorded in 2022. Presented with first quartile, median, mean, third quartile and N, overall and by roles/subgroups (solo, private firm roles, technical specializations, age, gender, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measures workload/billable productivity across practitioner categories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Average hourly billing rate in 2022 (Q33)
rubrics_metrics.description: Average hourly billing rate charged in 2022. Reported as mean, median, quartiles and N across respondent groups and subgroups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Key pricing metric segmented by role, location, specialty, and experience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dollar amount billed for legal services performed in 2022 (Q30)
rubrics_metrics.description: Total dollar amount billed for legal services in 2022. Presented with first quartile, median, mean, third quartile and N by practice subgroup.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Captures revenue production (dollars billed) for practitioners and groups.

rubrics_metrics.name: What percentage of your work is billed at a discounted hourly billing rate? (Q36)
rubrics_metrics.description: Percent of work billed at a discounted hourly rate. Reported as mean and median and N by practice category/role.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicates prevalence of discounted billing across practice types.

rubrics_metrics.name: Did your average hourly billing rate change in 2022? (Q34)
rubrics_metrics.description: Binary indicator (Yes/No) whether average hourly billing rate changed in 2022, with percentages and N by group.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shows frequency of rate adjustments in 2022 across roles.

rubrics_metrics.name: If your average hourly billing rate changed in 2022, how did it change? (Q35)
rubrics_metrics.description: Direction of change for average hourly billing rate among those reporting a change: Increase vs Decrease percentages and counts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Breaks down whether rates increased or decreased when a change occurred.

rubrics_metrics.name: What percentage of your work is billed under alternative fee arrangement? (Q37)
rubrics_metrics.description: Breakdown of percent of work billed under different alternative fee arrangements (flat fee for portfolio over a set period, flat fee per project, capped fee per project). Reported as mean percentages and N for respondent groups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shows adoption of alternative fee models and their relative prevalence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Percent of services in 2022 billed by basis (Q31)
rubrics_metrics.description: Percent of services billed (or to be billed) by billing basis: Hourly Billing, Predetermined Fee, Contingent Fee, Other Basis. Reported as mean percentages and N by group.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Profiles predominant billing bases across practice types.

rubrics_metrics.name: Average hours per week spent on business development (Q38)
rubrics_metrics.description: Average weekly hours devoted to business development. Reported as mean, median, quartiles and N across groups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicates time investment in marketing/business development by practitioners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Percent of time devoted to types of work (Q18)
rubrics_metrics.description: Percent of time respondents devote to specific types of work (e.g., IP prosecution work, Opinions/counseling prior to litigation, IP licensing, transactional work, IP litigation, post-grant proceedings, other dispute resolution, office management/administration, marketing/business development, pro bono, supervision/training, managing outside counsel). Reported as means and N, and also cross-tabulated by income levels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to analyze time-allocation across different IP work activities and how that correlates with income.

rubrics_metrics.name: Percent of time devoted to IP areas (Q16)
rubrics_metrics.description: Percent of time devoted to IP practice areas (Business Law, Copyrights, Foreign IP Law, General IP, Patents, Trade Secrets, Trademarks, Privacy/Cybersecurity, Other areas). Reported as means and N and cross-tabulated by income levels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Profiles concentration of practice by IP area and links area mix to income brackets.

rubrics_metrics.name: New priority US and PCT patent applications prepared and filed by you in 2022 (Q20)
rubrics_metrics.description: Number of new priority US and PCT patent applications prepared and filed by the respondent in 2022. Reported as mean, median, quartiles and N overall and by subgroups (location, technical specialization, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measures individual patent drafting/filing productivity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demographic and professional background indicators
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent background metrics such as admission to the Patent Bar (Yes/No), Age, Gender, Ethnicity, IP non-attorney experience (years), IP attorney experience (years), Highest non-law education (Bachelor's, Master's, Doctorate, Other). Presented as percentages, means, and counts for groups (e.g., Solo Practitioner, Private Firm Partner).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to profile workforce composition and correlate demographics/experience with economic indicators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Solo Practitioner-specific background and financial metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: A set of metrics presented specifically for Solo Practitioners: admitted to patent bar, age, gender, ethnicity, years of IP experience, highest non-law education, count, detailed income (Q13a), retirement contributions (Q14), expected income (Q15), percent time on work types (Q18), percent time on IP areas (Q16), billable hours (Q32), hourly rates (Q33), dollars billed (Q30), new priority applications filed (Q20). Each reported with distributional statistics (quartiles, mean, median, N) and many subgroup cross-tabs (years experience, location, technical specialization, age ranges, gender, degree, ethnicity, income brackets).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides granular breakdowns for solo practitioners to compare against other practice types and subgroups.
